_note: Hand transliteration of fixture7 into Devanagari — the gold-standard arm and the upper bound for the whole approach. Drafted by Claude and REVIEWED by the speaker on 2026-09-18: the phonetics were accepted as drafted, including the voiced sibilants (डज़, गिव्ज़, रिप्लेसेज़, मेज़र, लूज़िंग), and the only correction was to mirror the English hyphen in the number compounds — फोर्टी-सेवन and थर्टी-वन, previously spaced. The hyphen is the one character here that no existing fixture exercises: no Devanagari line in scripted_text.json or reference_text.json contains one, so the en->hi run that synthesized clean says nothing about it. If it is out of IndicF5's vocab it maps to index 0, which is a space, giving back exactly the spaced form it replaced — a safe failure, but confirm it with colab/vocab_check.py rather than assume it. Text is NFC-normalised, so nukta letters are stored decomposed (ज़ as ज + U+093C) — U+0958..U+095F are Unicode composition exclusions, so NFC pulls the precomposed forms apart rather than building them, and precomposed_nukta is empty on every row. devanagari_fraction counts only isalpha() characters, so the hyphen and the danda do not dilute it. Punctuation otherwise follows the Hindi gen-text convention in fixtures/scripted_text.json: commas and em dashes kept, sentence-final danda. That is a choice, not a finding — gen-text punctuation is its own variable (TRANSLITERATION_PLAN §4, phase 4). Where an English word already has a conventional Hindi spelling it is used verbatim rather than spelled afresh, because that is the form IndicF5's Hindi training text contains; the eight taken straight from the Hindi fixture are listed in from_hindi_fixture. Vocabulary coverage against IndicF5's vocab.txt has NOT been checked — run colab/vocab_check.py before synthesis, because an out-of-vocabulary character maps to index 0, which is a space, and is spoken as a pause rather than raising.
